expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: trialing has only trialEndsAt; active has only renewsAt; past_due has attempt/gracePeriodEndsAt/lastFailureAt; canceled has cancellation/accessEndsAt

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: Shows `assertNever` function definition and uses it in `isEntitled` switch with `default: return assertNever(sub);`

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Shows `transition()` function stub and explicitly states `readonly` everywhere makes it 'the only way to reach a new state'

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Has '## Misuse enumeration' table with 8 numbered hazards (C8, C2, F1, M3, C3/C1, F7, C9 mapped to catalog codes)

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Explicitly criticizes bag-of-optionals: '`{status, trialEndsAt?, ...}` claims **2⁶ = 64 states**. Four are real.' Then provides discriminated union as solution
